hook.line: AI engineering is the highest paying entry-level job in tech right now.
hook.visual: Black screen with a fixed white title on top; a 16:9 card on a grid background animates a purple bar chart of top tech salaries growing from zero.

beats.what: Bar chart 'Highest Paying Tech Jobs in 2026' animates in under a fixed series title
'Barrier To Entry' card with a striped boom gate that lifts
'The Conventional Roadmap' card with a progress line about to fill
Two cards: one stamped red 'IGNORED', the other '0 courses, started building'
'Day 1: Start Building.' in green over a dark code window for Developer 2
Glowing red '8 Months Later... 0 Callbacks' card
Side by side result: 4 certificates and 0 offers vs 3 public projects and $150,000
Cartoon superhero meme cutaway on 'the market pays for what you shipped'
'PROJECT-FIRST' badge over two resource cards (fast.ai, Python For Everybody)
Screenshot of the scikit-learn site as the next step; video ends mid-roadmap

why_it_works: Salary numbers on an animated chart in the first 2 s answer 'why should I care' before any explanation
Two-developer comparison with the same start and different outcomes turns advice into a story with a verdict
A new motion card about every 10 s (9.03 events/min with zero cuts) keeps the eye busy without a face
'Part 1' in the title and ending mid-roadmap pulls viewers to the next part
weaknesses: Content sits in a small 16:9 strip, leaving most of the vertical frame black
No spoken-word captions, so sound-off viewers only get the fixed title
No face (face share 0.053), so there is no personal trust signal
Ends abruptly with no follow or part 2 prompt
for_robert: Borrow the two-person comparison: Fred plays 'developer 1' who does it the slow way while Robert plays the winner, each with a big result card at the end.
